title: India Presents 2036 Olympics Bid to IOC, Betting on Ahmedabad
excerpt: Sports Minister Mansukh Mandaviya, P T Usha and P V Sindhu front Thursday's online pitch to the Future Host Commission, built on Ahmedabad's 2030 Commonwealth Games infrastructure and a run of 36 international events.
body:
• India presented its bid to host the 2036 Olympic Games to the IOC's Future Host Commission in an online session on Thursday, November 26.
  • The pitch centres on Ahmedabad — host of the 2030 Commonwealth Games — and on India's recent hosting record: 36 international competitions across more than 15 cities between January 2025 and June 2026, with 19 more secured for 2027 and 2028.
  • Six rivals are in the race: Germany, Hungary, Qatar, the Republic of Korea, South Africa and Türkiye. The IOC's preferred hosts are not due to be selected until mid-2029.
  • The presentation lands while the Indian Olympic Association is embroiled in a disputed election process that the IOC has publicly criticised.

India will make its case to host the 2036 Olympic Games on Thursday, November 26, in an online presentation before the International Olympic Committee's Future Host Commission — the first formal pitch of a bid that would bring the Olympics to the country for the first time. The presentation, reported by PTI, centres on Ahmedabad as the proposed host city and on India's record of staging international events.

Who is presenting, and what they will argue

The Indian delegation includes Sports Minister Mansukh Mandaviya, Sports Secretary Hari Ranjan Rao, outgoing Indian Olympic Association (IOA) president P T Usha, IOA Athletes Commission head and two-time Olympic medallist P V Sindhu, Gujarat Sports Minister Harsh Sanghavi and IOA chief executive Raghuram Iyer. "Our focus would be on our growing capabilities, newly-developed infrastructure and the past record of hosting international events," a source told PTI. Between January 2025 and June 2026, India hosted 36 international competitions across more than 15 cities, and it had secured 19 more events for 2027 and 2028.

Ahmedabad carries much of the argument. The city has already secured the 2030 Commonwealth Games, will host the World Police and Fire Games in 2029, and is developing the large-scale infrastructure that India says will be fully in place well before 2036 — giving the IOC a venue plan that is being built and tested at other events rather than drawn only on paper. India formally expressed interest in hosting the Games in 2024. So far, only Türkiye among the rival bidders has made its presentation, according to PTI's source.

The competition and the road to 2029

Seven countries are in continuous dialogue with the IOC over 2036: India, Germany, Hungary, Qatar, the Republic of Korea, South Africa and Türkiye. The IOC assesses bids on venue planning, athlete experience, funding, political and public support, delivery capability and long-term legacy. After Thursday's presentation, the IOC will run an anonymous survey of public views on India's bid, expected in the third week of December, feeding into an evaluation in March. The process then moves to a Strategic Dialogue phase, in which countries answer the Future Host Questionnaire and provide core financial guarantees, followed by a Targeted Dialogue phase in 2028. The IOC Executive Board is due to select preferred hosts by mid-2029, with the final election by the IOC Session.

The problem India cannot pitch around

The presentation comes at a difficult moment for the IOA. Usha recently withdrew from the presidential race after alleging that "external forces" were attempting to sabotage her candidature, and she asked the IOC to intervene; the IOC responded by calling for a free and fair election without interference, and this month expressed disappointment over what it called "extremely regrettable" schisms within the association, warning they were damaging the reputation of the Olympic movement in India. Governance is one of the IOC's stated assessment areas, so the election dispute is not a side story to the bid — it is part of what Thursday's audience will weigh.
